tables.title: Process capability levels

rows.Name: Incomplete process
rows.Semantic description: The process is not implemented or fails to achieve its process purpose.

rows.Name: Performed process
rows.Semantic description: The implemented process achieves its process purpose.

rows.Name: Managed process
rows.Semantic description: The performed process is implemented in a managed fashion and work products are established, controlled and maintained.

rows.Name: Established process
rows.Semantic description: The managed process uses a defined process capable of achieving its process outcomes.

rows.Name: Predictable process
rows.Semantic description: The established process operates predictively within defined limits; quantitative management identifies and addresses variation.

rows.Name: Innovating process
rows.Semantic description: The predictable process is continually improved to respond to organizational change.

tables.title: Process attributes
Rating scale

rows.Name: Not achieved
rows.Explicit interpretation: Little or no evidence of achievement of the defined process attribute.

rows.Name: Partially achieved
rows.Explicit interpretation: Some evidence of an approach and some achievement; some aspects may be unpredictable.

rows.Name: Largely achieved
rows.Explicit interpretation: Evidence of a systematic approach and significant achievement; some weaknesses may exist.

rows.Name: Fully achieved
rows.Explicit interpretation: Evidence of a complete and systematic approach and full achievement; no significant weaknesses.
